title: Kapok: Ancient Kapoks You Can Visit
meta_description: Singapore's kapok has an 11.55-metre girth, among the largest trunks on the city's heritage register. Three mapped from Lima to Honolulu.
intro: Kapok is a rainforest giant, native to tropical lowland forest where it pushes its crown above the canopy on wide buttress roots, which makes every one we map a tree standing somewhere unlikely. Singapore's, at the foot of Mount Faber, has an 11.55 metre girth, among the largest trunks on the city's entire heritage register. Honolulu's was planted around 1851 by the German physician William Hillebrand on what was then his own homestead, and is now the oldest tree in the botanical garden later built around it. Lima's grows in a green strip in San Isidro, a rainforest species holding on in a coastal desert city whose weather is mostly grey sea fog.
